implementation.source_lineage: The exact source used for the single compile and fresh saved-reader consumer; no post-consumer source change.

mathematical_sources.author: Jonathan Passant
mathematical_sources.title: Configurations and Erdos-Style Distance Problems
mathematical_sources.role: Author presentation defines the real-plane minimax pinned-distance function and includes the zero self-distance.

mathematical_sources.title: Distribution of pinned distance trees in the plane F_p^2
mathematical_sources.role: Dated distinction between the real-plane pinned problem and the unpinned result; its finite-field theorems are outside this consumer.

source_provenance.input_selection: One new Cartesian product {0,...,16} x {0,...,28}; no retained point configuration or prior pair enumeration was consumed.
source_provenance.status_boundary: No claim that the bounded source lookup establishes the best bound or full problem status in October 2026.

mathematical_contract.geometry: ordinary Euclidean distances between distinct integer-plane points; integer squared distances preserve equality and order
mathematical_contract.input_semantics: each axis is a nonempty finite set; duplicate input entries do not create repeated points
mathematical_contract.self_distance: zero is a distinct distance and has multiplicity one at every pin
mathematical_contract.coefficient_meaning: number of target points at that squared distance, including the pin when the value is zero
mathematical_contract.index_order: axis coordinates sorted increasingly; point ID = x_index * y_coordinate_count + y_index; distinct distances sorted numerically
mathematical_contract.ranks: zero-based; include_zero defaults to true for distance navigation

finite_extremal_consequence.explanation: The extremal function minimizes the maximum over all 493-point sets; this one set supplies an upper bound, not a universal lower bound or an optimum.

summary.convention: zero self-distance included once; positive-distance count is one smaller
summary.mathematical_scope: the supplied finite Cartesian product, not a universal pinned-distance lower bound

retained_consumer.runtime: fresh connected V8 module and saved-index reader; no compile call

requests.rank_choice: floor(saved positive-distance count / 2), the upper middle zero-based rank

execution_scope.full_output: All axis-pair witnesses, per-pin target references, distinct axis profiles, 135 profile-pair coefficient vectors, 38,610 convolution term records, summary extrema and eight query responses are retained.
execution_scope.arithmetic: Squared differences and convolution distance sums use BigInt; bounded multiplicities and counts use exact Number integers.
execution_scope.no_geometry_replay: The saved reader checks structure, indexes saved rows and materializes point references. It recomputes neither one-dimensional squared differences nor convolution terms.
source_inspected_unexercised_paths: signed or sparse coordinate inputs and duplicate normalization
absent distance, EXCLUDED_ZERO, out-of-range rank and end-of-page returns
reused circle cache and sourceProfile access
execution_scope.no_additional_runtime_claim: Unexercised branches were inspected in source, not covered by a separate synthetic suite.
execution_scope.timing_scope: One 50 ms compile observation, one 35 ms saved-index opening and one 1 ms query batch; these are environment observations, not statistical benchmarks.
execution_scope.theorem_boundary: The rectangle extrema argument holds for every full rectangular integer grid; the runtime here covers only the stated 17 by 29 input. The API does not settle the general pinned-distance problem.
